news.title: Women's football faces budget cuts, talent exodus ahead of World Cup playoffs
news.lede: The Dutch women’s national team is still to qualify for the World Cup, raising concerns. Budgets are shrinking, and talents are relocating abroad in large numbers, NU.nl reports. “We’re lagging behind the rest," said Leonne Stentler, a former Dutch international. “Although we see very good things in the Netherlands and have experienced some beautiful moments, I am concerned," former national team coach Sarina Wiegman said earlier this year at the Erdevisie Awards.

Italy legend Fabio Cannavaro has picked Paris Saint-Germain winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia as his preferred winner of the 2026 Ballon d'Or, dismissing high-profile rivals including Kylian Mbappe, Lionel Messi, and Ousmane Dembele in the process. The former Juventus and Real Madrid defender told Gazzetta dello Sport that his pick was rooted in Kvaratskhelia's performances during last season's UEFA Champions League, which he described as the clearest measure of individual brilliance. news.title: From U-17 World Cup to Brazil: Indian football keeps finding hope, but how long does it last?
news.lede: In October 2017, when I was 16, I walked into Salt Lake Stadium believing I was getting a glimpse of Indian football's future. The stadium had been transformed for the FIFA Under-17 World Cup, the stands were buzzing, and I was watching Brazil, England and Spain play on a stage that seemed a world away from the football infrastructure I had grown up seeing in India.Almost nine years later, I returned to the same ground, this time carrying a laptop and a journalist's notebook.The excitement of watching world-class football in my hometown was still there, but so did a question I had not thought of asking as a teenager. What happens after the big teams leave? October 28, 2017, remains a special day in my football memories.

news.title: Cruel ‘reality check’ key for Tillies stars to elevate World Cup auditions
news.lede: A cruel “reality check” from Germany could be the awakening the Matildas need heading into the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup, according to Craig Foster. Joe Montemurro needed little time to see the weaknesses in his team’s tactics, as Australia’s beloved national team suffered a 4-2 loss to Germany on Saturday. news.title: Four mega stadiums under construction now from £28bn beast to 115,000 seater World Cup venue
news.lede: Sports fans across the globe will soon get to grace a number of huge new stadiums with some ambitious plans already in the works. As clubs and countries vie for prestige on the international stage, a number of exciting stadium projects are aiming to bring in even more fans and greater revenues to their owners. The construction of new grounds can result from sports or clubs gaining immense popularity, or from nations seeking to offer a contemporary stadium design for an upcoming competition or tournament. That is certainly the case for some of the most exciting projects under construction at the moment, with some having already broken ground and hoping for grand openings in the next few years.

news.title: All 47 Saudi Pro League players selected for 2026 FIFA World Cup
news.lede: The 2026 FIFA World Cup will feature some of the biggest names in world football, and the Saudi Pro League is set to have a sizeable presence on the sport’s biggest stage. A total of 47 players from 18 national teams, including 25 representing Saudi Arabia, are contracted to Saudi Pro League clubs heading into the tournament, underlining the league’s growing influence beyond the Kingdom. That figure rises to 49 players from 19 nations when including Curaçao defender Juriën Gaari of Abha and Saudi Arabia goalkeeper Mohammed Al-Owais of Al-Ula, who both play outside the Saudi top flight. news.title: 5 Southeast Asian-based players going to 2026 FIFA World Cup
news.lede: The 2026 FIFA World Cup is set to bring together the world’s best players across the United States, Canada and Mexico from June 11 to July 19. While no Southeast Asian national team managed to qualify for the expanded 48-team tournament, the region will still have a presence on football’s biggest stage through several players currently plying their trade in the region. Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia are all represented, with Selangor, Terengganu, Port FC and Persib Bandung contributing players to World Cup squads. Several others also came close to securing places before final selections were announced.
